newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: SECOND BODY FOUND AT THREDBO DISASTER SITE

Police have confirmed a second body has been found in the wreckage of the flattened ski lodges at Thredbo, but rescue workers are having difficulty extracting it from the debris. The discovery brings the total number of bodies found to two.
Meanwhile, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has comforted friends and family of victims of the landslide.
Carr said after an inspection, that questions needed to be answered about the cause of the disaster. He said a coronial inquiry should throw light on the incident.
AUSTRALIA AND JAPAN AGREE TO WORK ON GREENHOUSE OUTCOME
Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer says Australia and Japan have agreed to work toward a realistic outcome on greenhouse gas emissions.
It is part of an Australia-Japan partnership agenda, which is due to be released later today.

Addressing the opening of an Australia-Japan committee meeting in Tokyo, Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said all issues on the partnership agenda were important, but a few stood out as particularly vital from Australia's point of view.
"Achieving a realistic and equitable outcome on climate change in Kyoto which takes into account both our countries' interests is one," he said.
Developed countries are to set new greenhouse gas emission targets at the climate change conference in Kyoto.
BEAZLEY SAYS WILSON SHOULD HAVE BEEN REAPPOINTED
Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley says Sir Ronald Wilson should have been reappointed to head the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission.
The head of the inquiry into the removal of Aboriginal children from their families, is ending his term of office as President of the Commission.
The High Court's rejection yesterday of a bid by nine so-called "stolen children" for compensation marked the final day of Sir Ronald's term.
Beazley said Sir Ronald should have been reappointed for at least the time it takes for an appropriate response to the Stolen Generation Report.
Beazley said the government's offer to Sir Ronald of an ongoing occasional involvement in human rights matters was inappropriate.
NEW MEDICARE FUNDING ARRANGEMENTS BY END OF THE YEAR
A draft proposal detailing the amount of money being demanded by the state and territory governments under new Medicare arrangements will be finalised by the end of the year.
Australian health ministers today held talks in Cairns, north Queensland, to discuss the new deal.
The current five year agreements between the Commonwealth and the states and territories run out next June.
Meeting chairman, Queensland Health Minister Mike Horan, said he is confident the Australian Health Care Agreement will be signed by mid-1988.
SUCCESS FOR PERTH MEDICAL TEAM IN BONE MARROW TRANSPLANT
A Perth medical team has become the first in Australia to successfully treat severe rhumatoid arthritis with a bone marrow transplant.
A 46-year-old Perth man, who was confined to his bed and an electric wheelchair with the affliction, can now walk again.
The medical team, from Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital, went ahead with the transplant after all other treatments failed to relieve the patient's symptoms.
But the hospital's head of Clinical Haematology, David Joske, said it is a risky treatment that would only work for people whose bones and joints are not severely damaged.
Doctor Joske said the treatment has a two to four per cent chance of fatality.
A national clinical trial of the treatment is underway.
ELLE RACING SYNDICATE CONCEDES IT'S OUT OF THE RACE
Western Australia will definitely not be represented in this year's Whitbread Round the World Yacht race.
The Elle Racing Syndicate has finally conceded it will not be mounting a challenge.

For months syndicate boss, John Harvey, has insisted he will be entering a boat, despite mounting problems which culminated in last month's decision by the State Government to sever its sponsorship deal.
Harvey claimed the WA Tourism Commission still owed A$500,000 but yesterday the Commission paid him A$100,000 saying that was the final settlement, a move which has angered him.
Mr Harvey said he will be seeking massive damages from the government and will be issuing writs this weekend.
DECISION RESERVED IN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY TRIBUNAL CASE
The Equal Opportunity Tribunal has reserved its decision on whether to hear a woman's complaint that she was not allowed to work at the Sydney Harbour Casino because of her partner's criminal record.
Mary-Anne Bignall has complained of discrimination on the grounds of marital status after the Casino Control Authority refused to give her a licence to work on the gambling tables.
The 32-year-old woman was told the reason was because of her de facto husband's criminal conviction.
The Authority's lawyer today asked the Tribunal to strike out the complaint, claiming it was not within its jurisdiction to hear the discrimination allegation.
